records.source: לְדָוִ֨ד׀בָּ֘ר֤וּךְ יְהוָ֨ה׀צוּרִ֗י הַֽמְלַמֵּ֣ד יָדַ֣י לַקְרָ֑ב אֶ֝צְבְּעוֹתַ֗י לַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: Of David. Blessed [be] YHWH, my rock, who trains my hands for battle, my fingers for war.
pieces: Of David. Blessed be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my rock, the one who teaches my hands to fight and my fingers to make war.

L.1: Of David. Blessed [be] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my rock, who trains my hands for battle, my fingers for war.

R.1: By David. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my rock! He trains my hands to fight in battle and my fingers to make war.

decisions.reason: As in 141:1, the title "Of David" and the first line are counted together as verse 1.

Verses 1-2 and 5-7 take up words from David's song of victory: "blessed be my rock" (18:47), "who trains my hands for war" (18:35), and the list of names for God in 18:3. The wording here follows Psalm 18 where the Hebrew is the same.

decisions.choice: my rock: my safe place and defense
decisions.reason: As in 18:3 (tsur), the rock is a high, safe place that enemies cannot reach.

decisions.choice: battle, war: close fighting and warfare
decisions.reason: The first word (qerav) is battle, close combat; the second (milchamah) is war.
To bless God is to praise him; Readable says "Praise", as in 18:47.

records.heading: A prayer for the king's victory

records.source: חַסְדִּ֥י וּמְצוּדָתִי֮ מִשְׂגַּבִּ֪י וּֽמְפַלְטִ֫י לִ֥י מָ֭גִנִּי וּב֣וֹ חָסִ֑יתִי הָרוֹדֵ֖ד עַמִּ֣י תַחְתָּֽי׃
records.gloss: My loyal love and my stronghold, my high refuge and my deliverer for me, my shield and in whom I take refuge, who subdues my people under me.
pieces: He is my loyal love and my stronghold, my tower on the heights and the one who sets me free, my shield, the one I shelter in, who brings my people under my rule.

L.2: My loyal love and my stronghold, my high refuge and my deliverer [who is] mine, my shield and [the one] in whom I take refuge, who subdues my people under me.

R.2: He loves me faithfully and protects me like a fort. He is like a tower high above my enemies, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rescues me. He protects me like a shield, and I run to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for safety. He makes my people obey me.

alternatives: peoples (some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient translations, as in 18:48)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "my people": God keeps the king's own people loyal to him. Some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient translations read "peoples", as in 18:48, where God brings nations under David's rule.

decisions.choice: my loyal love: the God who shows me loyal love
decisions.reason: God is called by what he gives, as in 59:11 and 59:18, "the God of my loyal love" (chesed). Literal and Balanced keep "loyal love", Readable "loves me faithfully", as in 5:8.
Stronghold, high refuge, deliverer, shield and "in whom I take refuge" are all from 18:3, and "subdues ... under me" is from 18:48.
Balanced begins with "He is" so the list of names reads as a sentence.

decisions.choice: like a fort; like a tower high above my enemies; like a shield
alternatives: my stronghold, my high refuge, my shield
decisions.reason: As in 18:3, Readable makes the pictures into comparisons.

records.gloss: YHWH, what [is] humankind that you know him, a son of man that you consider him?
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, what are {{gender:human beings|men}}, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} take notice of them, mere mortals, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give them a thought?

L.3: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, what [is] {{gender:a human|man}}, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know {{gender:them|him}}, {{gender:a mortal|the son of man}}, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} take thought of {{gender:them|him}}?

R.3: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, who are we people, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} even notice us? Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} think about human beings at all?

decisions.reason: The question echoes 8:5 (see also Job 7:17), with different verbs: "know" and "consider" instead of "remember" and "visit". The wording follows 8:5 where the Hebrew is the same. Here the question leads not to wonder at human glory, as in Psalm 8, but to how brief human life is (verse 4).

decisions.choice: know: take notice of, care for
decisions.reason: To know someone is to pay attention to them and care for them (1:6; 31:8).

decisions.choice: humankind, son of man: any human being
decisions.reason: 'Adam and ben 'enosh both mean a human being, weak and mortal. They do not refer to men rather than women.

records.source: אָ֭דָם לַהֶ֣בֶל דָּמָ֑ה יָ֝מָ֗יו כְּצֵ֣ל עוֹבֵֽר׃
records.gloss: Humankind to the breath is like; his days [are] like a shadow passing.
pieces: Human beings are like a breath; their days are a shadow sliding by.

L.4: {{gender:A human|Man}} is like a breath; {{gender:their|his}} days [are] like a passing shadow.

R.4: People are like a puff of air. Their lives pass by as quickly as a shadow.

decisions.choice: breath: a puff of air, something without weight
decisions.reason: The word (hevel) is vapor or breath, what quickly vanishes. It is the key word of Ecclesiastes ("breath of breaths").

decisions.choice: breath and shadow: as in 39:6-7 and 102:12
decisions.reason: The same pictures describe the shortness of life in 39:6-7, 102:12 and 109:23, and in Job 8:9 and 14:2.
As in verse 3, the words mean any human being; Balanced and Readable use the plural.

records.source: יְ֭הוָה הַט־שָׁמֶ֣יךָ וְתֵרֵ֑ד גַּ֖ע בֶּהָרִ֣ים וְֽיֶעֱשָֽׁנוּ׃
records.gloss: YHWH, bend your heavens and come down; touch the mountains, and they will smoke.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, bow {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} heavens low and come down; touch the mountains and make them pour out smoke.

L.5: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, bend {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} heavens and come down; touch the mountains, and they will smoke.

R.5: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, open the sky and come down. Touch the mountains and make them smoke.

decisions.choice: bend the heavens and come down: Psalm 18:10
decisions.reason: What 18:10 tells as past, the psalmist now asks for: "he bent the heavens and came down". The wording follows 18:10.

decisions.choice: the mountains smoke: as at Sinai
decisions.reason: When the LORD came down on Mount Sinai it was wrapped in smoke (Exodus 19:18); he touches the mountains and they smoke (104:32).
As in 18:10, Readable gives a plain picture of God coming down from the sky.

records.source: בְּר֣וֹק בָּ֭רָק וּתְפִיצֵ֑ם שְׁלַ֥ח חִ֝צֶּ֗יךָ וּתְהֻמֵּֽם׃
records.gloss: Flash lightning and scatter them; send your arrows and rout them.
pieces: Make the lightning flash and scatter the enemy; let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arrows fly and throw them into confusion.

L.6: Flash lightning and scatter them; send out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arrows and rout them.

R.6: Send flashes of lightning and make the enemy run away. Shoot {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arrows and leave them not knowing where to go.

decisions.choice: arrows that scatter and rout: Psalm 18:15
decisions.reason: 18:15 uses the same verbs: God sent out his arrows, scattered the enemy and routed them. Here the lightning itself may be God's arrows.
"Them" has not been named yet; they are the foreigners of verse 7.
As in 18:15, Balanced and Readable name who is scattered (m2).

records.source: שְׁלַ֥ח יָדֶ֗יךָ מִמָּ֫ר֥וֹם פְּצֵ֣נִי וְ֭הַצִּילֵנִי מִמַּ֣יִם רַבִּ֑ים מִ֝יַּ֗ד בְּנֵ֣י נֵכָֽר׃
records.gloss: Stretch out your hands from on high; set me free and deliver me from waters many, from [the] hand of sons of foreignness,
pieces: Reach out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands from on high; free me and pull me out of deep waters, out of the grip of foreigners,

L.7: Stretch out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands from on high; set me free and rescue me from many waters, from [the] hand of sons of foreign lands,

R.7: Reach down from heaven and pull me out of the deep water. Rescue me from the power of foreigners.

decisions.choice: from on high, out of many waters: Psalm 18:17
decisions.reason: 18:17 tells how God reached down from on high and drew David out of many waters. The deep waters are a picture of overwhelming danger (69:2-3).
As in 18:45-46, people from other nations, here enemies of the king.
Verse 8 describes the foreigners, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.
The hand stands for power; Readable says so.

records.source: אֲשֶׁ֣ר פִּ֭יהֶם דִּבֶּר־שָׁ֑וְא וִֽ֝ימִינָ֗ם יְמִ֣ין שָֽׁקֶר׃
records.gloss: whose mouth speaks falsehood, and their right hand [is] a right hand of deceit.
pieces: who speak nothing but lies with their mouths, and whose right hand is raised to swear what is false.

L.8: whose mouth speaks falsehood, and their right hand [is] a right hand of deceit.

R.8: They tell lies. Even when they raise their right hand and promise, they do not tell the truth.

decisions.choice: a right hand of deceit: a false oath
decisions.reason: The right hand was raised to swear an oath (Genesis 14:22; Deuteronomy 32:40). Their oaths and treaties cannot be trusted.
The word (shaw') is emptiness, what is false and worthless (12:3; 41:7).

decisions.choice: raised to swear (B); raise ... and promise (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the right hand is doing (m1).

records.source: אֱֽלֹהִ֗ים שִׁ֣יר חָ֭דָשׁ אָשִׁ֣ירָה לָּ֑ךְ בְּנֵ֥בֶל עָ֝שׂ֗וֹר אֲזַמְּרָה־לָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: God, a song new I will sing to you; on a harp of ten I will make music to you,
pieces: God, I will sing {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} a new song; I will play music for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} on the ten-stringed harp,

L.9: God, a new song I will sing to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; on a harp of ten [strings] I will make music to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}},

R.9: God, I will sing {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} a new song. I will play music for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} on a harp with ten strings.

decisions.reason: A new song celebrates a new act of rescue (33:3; 40:4; 96:1; 98:1; 149:1).

decisions.choice: harp of ten: a ten-stringed instrument
decisions.reason: As in 33:2, the nevel was a stringed instrument, here with ten strings.
Here the psalm uses "God" ('Elohim), the only time it does not use the divine name in address.
Verse 10 goes on to describe God, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.source: הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן תְּשׁוּעָ֗ה לַמְּלָ֫כִ֥ים הַ֭פּוֹצֶה אֶת־דָּוִ֥ד עַבְדּ֗וֹ מֵחֶ֥רֶב רָעָֽה׃
records.gloss: who gives salvation to kings, who sets free David his servant from [the] evil sword.
pieces: the one who gives victory to kings, who snatches {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant David away from the cruel sword.

L.10: who gives salvation to kings, who sets free David {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant from [the] evil sword.

R.10: You are the one who makes kings win their battles. You rescue {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant David from the deadly sword.

decisions.reason: The word (teshu'ah) is rescue or deliverance, which in battle means victory (18:51; 33:17).

decisions.choice: David his servant: as in 18:1 and 18:51
decisions.reason: Psalm 18 opens by calling David "the servant of the LORD" and closes with God's saving acts for "his king ... David".

decisions.choice: his servant: God spoken of, then addressed
decisions.reason: The psalm speaks to God (verse 9) and then about him ("his servant"); both are the same God.

decisions.choice: You are the one ... your servant
decisions.reason: Readable keeps speaking to God, as verse 9 does, so the sentence can stand on its own.

records.source: פְּצֵ֥נִי וְהַצִּילֵנִי֮ מִיַּ֪ד בְּֽנֵי־נֵ֫כָ֥ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר פִּ֭יהֶם דִּבֶּר־שָׁ֑וְא וִֽ֝ימִינָ֗ם יְמִ֣ין שָֽׁקֶר׃
records.gloss: Set me free and deliver me from [the] hand of sons of foreignness, whose mouth speaks falsehood, and their right hand [is] a right hand of deceit.
pieces: Free me and pull me out of the grip of foreigners, who speak nothing but lies with their mouths, and whose right hand is raised to swear what is false.

L.11: Set me free and rescue me from [the] hand of sons of foreign lands, whose mouth speaks falsehood, and their right hand [is] a right hand of deceit.

R.11: Rescue me from the power of foreigners. They tell lies. Even when they raise their right hand and promise, they do not tell the truth.

decisions.reason: This verse repeats the plea of verses 7-8 almost word for word, and is rendered the same way.
As in verse 8.

decisions.choice: raised to swear (B); raise ... and promise (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.

records.source: אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּנֵ֨ינוּ׀כִּנְטִעִים֮ מְגֻדָּלִ֪ים בִּֽנְעוּרֵ֫יהֶ֥ם בְּנוֹתֵ֥ינוּ כְזָוִיֹּ֑ת מְ֝חֻטָּב֗וֹת תַּבְנִ֥ית הֵיכָֽל׃
records.gloss: That our sons [are] like plants grown up in their youth, our daughters like corner pillars carved [after the] pattern of a palace,
pieces: Then may our sons be like saplings grown tall while they are still young, and our daughters like corner columns carved for a royal house,

L.12: So that our sons [may be] like plants grown large in their youth, our daughters like corner pillars carved [after the] pattern of a palace,

R.12: Then may our sons grow tall and strong while they are young, like healthy young trees. May our daughters be like beautiful carved pillars in a palace.

decisions.choice: that: what will follow the rescue
decisions.reason: The verse begins with a word ('asher) that usually means "who" or "that". Here it most likely introduces the blessing hoped for once the king is rescued (verse 11): "so that". Verses 12-14 describe a people at peace, and verse 15 calls such a people blessed.

decisions.choice: corner pillars carved for a palace
decisions.reason: Corner pieces of fine buildings were carved with care. The daughters are pictured as strong, graceful and beautiful.
The word (neti'im) is something planted. Healthy young plants are a picture of strong growth (128:3).
Balanced and Readable express the hope as a wish, which is the sense of "so that" here (m1).

records.source: מְזָוֵ֣ינוּ מְלֵאִים֮ מְפִיקִ֥ים מִזַּ֗ן אֶ֫ל־זַ֥ן צֹאונֵ֣נוּ מַ֭אֲלִיפוֹת מְרֻבָּב֗וֹת בְּחוּצוֹתֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: our granaries full, providing from kind to kind; our flocks producing thousands, made ten thousands in our open places,
pieces: our storehouses full, supplying every kind of food, our flocks multiplying into the thousands, tens of thousands across our pastures,

L.13: our barns full, supplying from kind to kind; our flocks producing thousands, ten thousands in our open fields,

R.13: May our barns be full of all kinds of food. May our sheep have so many lambs that there are thousands and thousands of them in our fields.

decisions.choice: from kind to kind: food of every kind
decisions.reason: The phrase (mizzan 'el zan) is found only here; it means every kind of produce.
The word (tso'n) covers sheep and goats together.

decisions.choice: our open places: the fields outside the town
decisions.reason: The word (chutsot) is the space outside, here the open country where flocks graze.

records.source: אַלּוּפֵ֗ינוּ מְֽסֻבָּ֫לִ֥ים אֵֽין־פֶּ֭רֶץ וְאֵ֣ין יוֹצֵ֑את וְאֵ֥ין צְ֝וָחָ֗ה בִּרְחֹבֹתֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: our cattle laden; no breach and no going out, and no outcry in our open places.
pieces: our cattle heavy with young. May there be no breach in our walls, no going out into exile, no cry of distress in our streets.

L.14: our cattle heavy laden; [there is] no breach and no going out, and no outcry in our streets.

R.14: May our cows have many calves. May no enemy break through our walls. May none of us be taken away as captives. May no one cry out in pain in our city streets.

decisions.reason: The word (mesubbalim) means carrying a load. Next to the flocks of verse 13 it most likely means cows heavy with calves.

decisions.choice: no breach and no going out: no enemy breaking in, no one led away captive
alternatives: no miscarriage and no loss (of the cattle)
decisions.reason: The words are short and can be read two ways. They may continue the picture of the herds (no miscarrying, no loss of young), or describe the city at peace: no breach in the walls and no going out into exile. The cry in the streets that follows fits the second.
The word (tsewachah) is a loud cry of grief or alarm (Isaiah 24:11; Jeremiah 14:2).

alternatives: no breach and no going out
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the breach and the going out are (m2).

records.source: אַשְׁרֵ֣י הָ֭עָם שֶׁכָּ֣כָה לּ֑וֹ אַֽשְׁרֵ֥י הָ֝עָ֗ם שֶׁיֲהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽיו׃
records.gloss: How blessed the people that thus [is] to it; how blessed the people whose God [is] YHWH.
pieces: How blessed the people who live like this! How blessed the people who have {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as their God!

L.15: How blessed [is] the people for whom [it is] so; how blessed [is] the people whose God [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!

R.15: Life is truly good for people who have all this. Life is truly good for people who have {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as their God.

decisions.choice: how blessed: how truly well off
decisions.reason: As in 1:1 ('ashre): a life that is truly good.

decisions.choice: the people whose God is the LORD: 33:12
decisions.reason: 33:12 says the same of the nation whose God is the LORD. The second line gives the reason for the first: the good things of verses 12-14 come from the LORD.
As in 1:1.
